text:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing a single tenant (t42) steadily grow KV residency for 48h and pushing other tenants toward OOMs.
sam: How big is the growth? raw numbers please.
maya: Baseline per-tenant max_residency ~= 1.2GB. t42 climbed to ~4.1GB over 48h. Growth correlates with long-context demo traffic (seq len spikes).
devon: Any fragmentation/pagewalk spikes when that happens? grabbed a heap snapshot at 11:02.
maya: Yes — fragmentation rose a lot. pprof summary pasted below.
```
pprof heap: total=12.3GB
  tcache-resident: 6.4GB
  kv-fragments: 3.5GB (28%)
  active-kv: 2.4GB
```
ryan: Was eviction disabled for that tenant or misconfigured? I thought soft-quota would reclaim.
elena: Soft quota was OFF for the dedicated test pool. For hosted the TTL on entries was mis-set (infinite for some paths).
maya: Repro steps I used: spawn 10 synthetic sessions that append ~1k tokens to the context every minute. Command:
```
python perf_sim.py --tenant t42 --sessions 10 --ctx-growth 1000 --duration 48h
```
devon: Quick bench from the run: 99p latency +12ms; cache hit-rate aggregate dropped from 92% -> 67%; small tenants hit-rate fell to ~54% while t42 stayed at 98%. :frowning: 
maya: Root cause hypothesis: variable-sized KV entries cause fragmentation + poor reuse. Free holes are often too small/aligned for subsequent entries, so footprint monotonically grows.
sam: Two short-term mitigations: 1) enable per-tenant hard caps (reject heavy writes) 2) background defrag sweep that coalesces free pages into larger slots. Which do we want to try first?
ryan: I vote hard cap first (quick rollbackable), then defrag. Also consider per-size-class slab allocator (medium term).
elena: Ran a 6h sim with per-tenant cap=1.5GB + burst_allowance=500MB (5m). Results: prevented others' hit-rate from dropping below 70%, t42 experienced periodic throttles but overall latency stable.
maya: infra-bot triggered an eviction sweep during test, log snippet:
infra-bot: eviction-sweeper: tenant=t42 reclaimed=1.6GB reason=soft-cap-exceed time=2026-03-16T11:24:03Z
devon: Implementation notes: defrag costs GPU cycles; should run on low-load windows and be interruptible. Also need metrics: fragments_by_size, free_runs_histogram.
sam: For fairness, we should implement tenant-weighted eviction: floor guaranteed residency + dynamic share for bursts. That avoids starving small tenants.
ryan: Agreed. Also add an alert if a tenant grows > 2x baseline in 24h (auto-create incident).
elena: I'll open a dedicated perf experiment & CI run to validate defrag + slab allocator on longctx traces.
maya: Short term action items:
  - elena: enable per-tenant hard caps in hosted staging (1.5GB) by EOD — and turn on alert for growth >2x (OWNED)
  - devon: prototype background defrag sweep (best-effort, preemption-friendly) — PR by Thu
  - sam: update oncall runbook (eviction indicators + rollback steps)
  - ryan: simulation harness: add fragments_by_size and tenant-weighted eviction model

Please ack when assigned. :eyes:
ryan: Acked, will add metrics.
devon: Acked, prototyping now.
elena: Acked, will flip staging and run smoke tests.
sam: Acked, will update runbook and post short postmortem template after staging test.
maya: Thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10:30 to review defrag perf and rollout plan. :thumbsup:
